newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile close to reaching inflation target-Aninat.
newsitem.headline: Chile close to reaching inflation target-Aninat.

text.p: Chile is close to achieving its inflation target for the year with the central bank's year-long belt-tightening showing positive results, said Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat.
Consumer prices rose 0.4 percent last month which brought inflation rate to 6.6 percent over the last 12 months.
"We are only just short of reaching our target of 6.5 percent (for 1996)," Aninat told reporters.

Despite the slowdown in inflation in recent months, the bank's restrictive monetary policy will continue into the first half of next year until Chile's robust economic growth has been brought firmly under control, he said.
"The adjustment should not continue further than the first half of 1997," said Aninat.
The government has set an inflation target of 5.5 percent for next year. Consumer prices rose 8.2 percent in 1995.
